"Just because someone stumbles and loses their path, doesn't mean they're lost forever."

The core of the X-Men story still shines through, good performances, almost gleeful in the sort of “turn your brain off” bliss that comes from slicing people up.

singleSourced.value: for crafting unlocked suits; whiskey bottles that unlock upgrades;
singleSourced.context: The collectibles, for instance, feel perhaps aptly like something from a distant and half-remembered gaming past: identikit crates that give you +50 "material" for crafting unlocked suits; whiskey bottles that unlock upgrades; "caches" that are just glowing blue or red non-entities dotted around the place that you whack for XP.
The fact that the game is 10-20 hours or so makes it worth the $70 to me and I feel like everyone will have a different take on the story.
Most of the reviews I'm reading are starting to echo "PlayStation style of game fatigue" and Marvel fatigue.
